newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rail transit signs 2.0 bln rgt facilities.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rail transit signs 2.0 bln rgt facilities.

text.p: A Malaysian company which is developing a light rail transit system has signed a 2.0 billion ringgit Islamic and conventional project financing facilities with a syndicate of 27 domestic institutions, Bank Bumiputra Malaysia Bhd said on Wednesday.

Projek Usahasama Transit Ringan Automatik Sdn Bhd (PUTRA) signed a 1.0 billion ringgit Islamic tranche arranged by Commerce International Merchant Bankers Bhd, Commerce MGI Sdn Bhd and Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd.
Another 1.0 billion ringgit conventional tranche was arranged by Bank Bumiputra.
PUTRA is developing Malaysia's second light rail transit system in and around capital Kuala Lumpur.
The project's capital expenditure for the 29 km long system is estimated at 4.35 billion ringgit with full completion targeted in June 1999.
It will be part financed by equity, the syndicated Islamic and conventional project financing facilities and from PUTRA's internal funds.
The tenor for the conventional tranche is for a period of 15 years which include a five-year grace period, Bank Bumiputra said in a statement.

Under the Islamic facility, called istisna, the financiers will purchase the original contract to supply goods and services to PUTRA from the supplier, and then sell the goods to PUTRA at a fixed profit mark-up.
The payment by PUTRA for the goods is on a deferred payment basis for four years, thus offering PUTRA a fixed rate.

The istisna facility will be converted into an ijara facility after the construction stage. In this transaction, the financiers will purchase the goods which are delivered to PUTRA under the istisna facility, and subsequently lease the goods to PUTRA for a variable rental payments over 11 years.
